history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN: the CSV name 'Bilaspur Devi Temple' has NO documented referent in Dhamtari — no temple by that name exists in any source found after repeated searching. This file is a provisional mapping to Bilai Mata Mandir, the major Devi shrine and presiding deity of Dhamtari city, as the most likely intended temple; the CSV name may be a transcription corruption of 'Bilai Mata'. Legend: the site was dense forest where King Narhar Deo, out hunting, found his horses halted by a herd of cats (bilai) gathered on a stone; when he tried to move the stone, water flowed, and the goddess appeared in his dream ordering worship at that spot; the idol then rose from the earth on its own (swayambhu) and is believed to still be rising slowly. Counted among the five Shaktipeeths of the state. 108 goats were sacrificed here during Navratri from King Narhar Dev's reign until ~1938, when the practice was abolished and raw pumpkin is now offered. A divine stepwell inside the premises supports the temple's antiquity claims.

town_description: Dhamtari is a city and district headquarters in Chhattisgarh on the Mahanadi, about 78 km from Raipur. It is the gateway to the Gangrel (Ravishankar) reservoir and Sitanadi Wildlife Sanctuary, and is a major regional centre of Shakti worship.
